system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft vs. Buyer Playbook

**Status note:** The Seller's cover note calls its positions "settled at principal level", "FINAL", "market standard" and "not intended to be re-opened". Under playbook §0.4 and §6.3 those labels don't bind us. Nothing in the file shows Amelia Frost or the buyer deal team has agreed any of these positions. The market-context claims are also unverified. I've treated the whole Seller package as an opening position to be tested, not an agreed bargain.

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Topic | Seller draft | Our playbook | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start. 20% is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written authority, none given | Seller is already at our fallback, without authority |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only recoverable | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | 5x higher, and loses the first-dollar mechanic |
| General claims period (12/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 needs Frost approval) | Seller is at our fallback |
| Fundamental/Title (general) | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Fundamental |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum enforceable extent | No fraud carve-out |
| Disclosure (Sch. 7; DL 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject deemed disclosure | Fundamental |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Bars claims for anything Buyer or advisers "had knowledge" of or "discoverable" from data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Fundamental |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence of conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Fundamental |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release "to be provided following Completion" | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Fundamental |
| Bonuses / funds flow | DD-005 AUD 420,000 not in funds flow; "a matter for the Seller" | Must be a specific line item or seller-funded; on-costs included | Fundamental |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment, "adequate" | Broaden the narrow indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 unverified | Departure |
| Export/privacy (4.6; Sch. 6; DL 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way | Seller's materiality view is an assertion we shouldn't adopt |
| Sandbar renewals (DL 8) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction | Departure, needs assessment |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Open. No unlimited liability and no resolution assumed | Unresolved; the Seller can't treat them as settled |
| Title (DL 10) | DD-012 share register is sufficient evidence | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is an internal source only | Departure |

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

**a. Caps, basket and time limits.** The Seller has moved to the edges of our fallback positions and set the de minimis and basket at five times our opening numbers. Converted to real terms, the basket is about 1% of price, which is the Seller's own "market" figure. Our playbook sets the basket at about 0.2% of price with first-dollar recovery. The "excess only" basket, combined with a AUD 25,000 de minimis, could leave a large share of genuine warranty losses unrecoverable. The 18-month claims period also cuts short the window for a full financial year-end audit cycle.

**b. Fundamental/Title pulled into the general regime.** This is the most serious structural issue. Subjecting title and capacity to the general caps, time limits and knowledge bar means that a title defect could be capped at AUD 4.8m and time-barred after 18 months. Title needs a separate regime with a 100% cap and at least six years. The Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale does not justify this.

**c. Fraud carve-out and exclusivity.** Applying the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to "all Claims of any nature" would apply them to fraud. The playbook requires carve-outs to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive this. This should be treated as a non-negotiable point.

**d. Disclosure and buyer knowledge.** Clause 1.1 of the Disclosure Letter discloses every fact in the data room, and 8.3 bars claims for matters discoverable from it. Together they would make the Buyer carry the risk of anything in the data room, which defeats specific warranty protection. Our disclosure position is specific fair disclosure only, with no blanket knowledge exclusion.

**e. Completion conditions and payoff.**
- *Bluefen* is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m). The Seller has not provided a final written consent, and its "consent on delivery" and "reasonable endeavours" approach would let Completion proceed without effective consent. Our requirement is effective consent plus evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion.
- *Riverlark* carries AUD 3.2m of debt. Releasing security after Completion, with no payout from the funds, leaves our exposure open. Repayment should be direct from Completion funds.
- *Bonuses* of AUD 420,000 are missing from the funds flow. The "matter for the Seller" wording does not make them a seller liability, and the on-costs (payroll tax, super) are unquantified. We should require either a specific line item in the funds flow or express seller funding, including on-costs.

**f. Specific risks.**
- *Ironquay:* The indemnity covers only the SOW3 fee (AUD 180,000, unverified). We need the broader indemnity and the SOW3 cure preserved, and proof of payment or confirmatory assignment (DD-004 clause 7.3).
- *DD-006 export incident:* The Seller's "not expected to be material" view is an assertion. The facts are ~1,240 records, unknown access, and unresolved notification. We should require log preservation, an investigation, and regular updates, and make no assumption about breach or loss either way.
- *Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000):* These need assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. They should not be automatically treated as debt or deducted from price.

**g. Tax and IP.** These are open and cannot be folded into the general regime. Treat them as separate heads of claim with separate positions to be negotiated.

**h. Title evidence.** DD-012 is the Seller's own share register. It is a useful starting point, but we need independent evidence of ownership, encumbrances and authority.

**i. Items not in the playbook.** The office lease (DD-007) notification obligation, the Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009), and the Seller's disclaimers in DL 1.4 and 11 should be reviewed by the deal team. I have not analysed them against a playbook position, so I'm flagging them only.

## 3. Recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller package as drafted.** Note in writing that the "FINAL" and "settled" labels are not accepted, and that no positions have been agreed.
2. **Reset the general regime:** 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 first-dollar basket, 24 months. Do not offer the 20% / 18-month fallback without written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft.
3. **Split out Fundamental/Title:** 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Add a fraud carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
5. **Delete the data-room, public-register and blanket buyer-knowledge provisions.** Require specific disclosure, and any knowledge qualifier must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry.
6. **Make Bluefen a condition precedent:** effective written consent and evidence that its conditions are met before Completion.
7. **Require Riverlark payout** from Completion funds, with releases delivered at Completion. Any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
8. **Fix the funds flow** to include the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs, or require express seller funding.
9. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** and keep the SOW3 cure. Require proof of SOW3 payment status.
10. **For DD-006,** require log preservation, investigation and regular updates. Do not accept the "not material" characterisation.
11. **For Sandbar,** require an assessment of each renewal. No automatic debt treatment or price deduction.
12. **Keep Tax and IP open** as separate heads of claim.
13. **Require independent title evidence** beyond DD-012.
14. **Confirm authority:** verify through our internal process what, if anything, has been agreed at principal level before responding, and do not rely on the Seller's cover-note assertions.
=== END ADVICE ===
